Subject: Dedicated pool sizing — initial numbers

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our internal ask, I’m sharing a quick snapshot of the production workload so you can advise on committed GPU sizing and whether a hybrid reserved/burst model makes sense. High-level:~
- Average QPS: 35 requests/sec (peaks to ~120 r/s over 10–15 minute windows)
- Average input tokens: 120; average output tokens: 240 (prompt + response ~360 tokens)
- 95% of requests are chat-style with 2–5 turns preserved in KV cache (effective context window ~3k tokens)
- Target p95 latency: < 200ms for response-first-token; p99 soft target 350ms
- Typical concurrency: sustained 200 active sessions, spikes to ~700
- Primary model: open-llama-70B-8bit-q4; fallback to open-llama-13B for lower latency/time-of-day bursts

We’ll attach the CSV with per-hour traffic and a short doc with a handful of representative prompts. Our procurement team wants a 12-month reserved commit but will need discounts and a defined burst policy.

Q: What committed pool size do you recommend for predictable throughput without overspending? Also — what discount tiers apply at ~48–96 GPU commit levels, and how does bursting onto shared capacity work under the SLA?

Best,
Eliot
Ops Lead, Orion AI

Thanks Eliot — helpful data. Looping in Marissa (solutions) and Aditya (inference) to validate sizing and latency expectations. Quick thoughts below and we’ll follow with a formal sizing and pricing note by EOD tomorrow.

Preliminary take:
- Sustained 35 QPS with 360 tokens/request => ~12.6k tokens/sec sustained (~756k tokens/min).
- Peaks at 120 QPS pushes tokens/sec to ~43.2k — that’s the key driver for GPU parallelism and KV cache memory.
- For open-llama-70B at 8-bit on H100-class instances we expect ~40–60 tokens/sec per GPU for end-to-end p95 under 200ms given short-generation tails; numbers vary with sequence length.

Ballpark recommendation (subject to SE confirmation):
- Reserved commit: 24 H100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (gives headroom for sustained load + 2x autoscale buffer inside the pool)
- Burst policy: allow up to 2x burst onto shared-hosted capacity with guaranteed priority routing; bursts above that would fall back to the 13B variant.

Pricing/discount ask: we can do a tiered discount at commit bands (24, 48, 96 GPUs). For a 12-month commit at 24 GPUs we can offer a 18% discount off list; at 48 GPUs 26%; 96 GPUs 33% — exact numbers formalized in the proposal.

Marissa/Aditya — can you confirm tokens/sec per GPU assumptions for the 70B 8-bit baseline and memory footprint for the 3k token working set?

-Neha

On Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 12:05 PM Neha Kapoor wrote:
> Marissa/Aditya — can you confirm tokens/sec per GPU assumptions for the 70B 8-bit baseline and memory footprint for the 3k token working set?

Hi all — dug into the CSV and ran a couple of synthetic traces against our perf bench. Summary below; happy to jump on a short call to walk numbers.

Perf assumptions (70B 8-bit, optimized kernels on H100 80GB):
- Median tokens/sec per GPU: 52 t/s for single-stream (1 request) with minimal batching.
- Concurrent multi-stream throughput: with continuous batching and 8 concurrent streams per GPU, aggregate ~350 t/s per GPU (best-effort batching for chat workloads).
- KV cache memory: ~10–12GB per session for a 3k token working set when using our sparse-KV packing; per-GPU session capacity ~6–8 sessions for the 70B model (higher for 13B).

Sizing note: given Orion’s sustained token rate (~12.6k t/s) and expected concurrency profile, 24 GPUs (as Neha suggested) would cover sustained traffic if we enable efficient batching (continuous batching + prefix caching). However, the 120 QPS bursts (43.2k t/s) would require either:
- Burst to shared capacity (~40–60 GPUs worth of hosted capacity) OR
- Automatic per-request fallback to 13B variant for low-latency responses during spikes.

Operational recommendation:
- Commit to 24 H100-equivalent GPUs for the Dedicated pool (handles steady-state + modest growth).
- Configure burst policy: allow automated burst up to 48 GPUs (mix of dedicated + shared) with prioritized routing and cost-controls; above 48 trigger automatic model-fallback to 13B.
- Provide an uplift buffer of 10% headroom in the commit for autoscaling margin during maintenance windows.

I’ll add a short worksheet with the math to the Drive link.

Quick engineering caveat and SLA note — sending from infra for visibility.

Caveat: tokens/sec benchmarks are sensitive to prompt distribution and end-token sampling patterns. If Orion often has long responses (400–800 output tokens) during certain flows, per-GPU t/s will drop ~20–35%. We should identify the 10% of traffic that produces long tails and decide if those can be routed to a smaller model or scheduled off-peak.

SLA / burst specifics:
- For a reserved 12-month, 24-GPU commit + burst policy up to 48 GPUs, we can guarantee:
  - 99.9% uptime for the Dedicated pool control plane
  - Throughput guarantee: sustained throughput for the committed GPUs (we commit to serving sustained tokens/sec equivalent to the retained commit; p95 latency SLOs will be met within committed capacity and configured batching thresholds)
  - Burst capacity onto shared-hosted is best-effort but Redwood will provide prioritized queueing up to the agreed burst cap; excess beyond burst is subject to a degradation policy with fallback model routing.

Operational ask for final quote: please confirm 1) acceptable p99 latency ceiling, 2) whether Orion requires guaranteed burst credit billing (i.e., pre-paid burst units) or pay-as-you-go billing for burst minutes. That will change discount structure slightly.

-Aditya

Eliot — thanks for the patience. Quick summary + pricing path forward: 

Summary recommendation (final):
- Recommended Reserved Commit: 24 H100-equivalent GPUs (12-month term) with 10% headroom.
- Burst policy: allow up to 48 GPU capacity (mix of dedicated + prioritized hosted) with automatic model-fallback to 13B beyond that.
- Discount: 20% on committed compute for 12-month term at 24 GPUs (we’ve moved slightly from the ballpark to a firm proposal: 20% today, scale to 28% at 48 GPUs, 34% at 96 GPUs).
- Billing for burst: pay-as-you-go for minutes on shared capacity by default; optional pre-purchased burst credits available at a 12% savings — let me know if procurement prefers credits.

Next steps:
1) I’ll share a draft quote and SLA addendum (attached: draft_sla_commit_terms.pdf).
2) If Orion signs, we onboard SRE/CS and schedule a 2-week ramp to verify traffic shaping and KV cache tuning.
3) Marissa will provide the workload worksheet and a short runbook for burst/fallback behaviors.

Could you confirm procurement preference on burst-credit prepay and whether you want a 2- or 4-week ramp period? Happy to hop on a call early next week to finalize.

Best,
